paper_metadata.title: Quantum Circuits for the Black-Scholes equations via Schrödingerisation

summary: The paper develops gate-based Schrödingerisation circuits for the Black-Scholes PDE in 1D and d dimensions, with Qiskit statevector simulations validating the method on small instances. Reported examples include nx=6, np=4/5/6 for the 1D case and nx=8, np=7 for a 2D cash-or-nothing option, with the smoother auxiliary initial condition achieving L2 errors of 2.925e-01, 7.540e-02, and 2.060e-02 and observed convergence orders of 1.96 and 1.88.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit simulation of the one-dimensional Black-Scholes equation using Schrödingerisation, validated numerically in Qiskit for different spatial and auxiliary-grid resolutions.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation-based quantum simulation of the 1D Black-Scholes PDE
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared from the discretized option payoff; two initial conditions tested: the direct discretized initial value and a smoother auxiliary initial function g(p).

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The discretized PDE state is mapped to computational basis states over the x-register (nx+1 qubits including boundary/auxiliary handling) and p-register (np qubits). The solution is recovered by inverse QFT and projection onto a selected p-state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the Black-Scholes PDE ∂w/∂t + r s ∂w/∂s + (σ^2 s^2 /2) ∂^2w/∂s^2 = r w via Schrödingerisation after variable transform and finite-difference discretization.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Dirichlet or mixed boundary conditions are incorporated through boundary terms and dilation; projection onto a selected auxiliary p-state is used to recover the original solution.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_BS = C1 ⊗ Dη + C2 ⊗ I^{⊗np} (discretized Hermitian Hamiltonian after Schrödingerisation)

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under the 1D Black-Scholes model.

dataset_specification.benchmark_name: Analytical Black-Scholes solution used as reference
dataset_specification.preprocessing: Log-price transform s = e^x; truncation to [L,R]; finite-difference discretization in x and p.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Parameters in Example 6.1: T=1, r=0.02, σ=0.3, K=30, smin=10^-4, smax=10K, x∈[ln(10^-4), ln(10K)], p∈[-4π,4π]. Two initial conditions were used, including a smoother g(p) to improve convergence.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical comparison against the exact Black-Scholes formula and classical finite-difference/matrix-exponential reference; convergence assessed for nx=6 with np=4,5,6 and for nx=5,6 with np=6; runtime and RAM reported for simulations.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical finite-difference ODE solve / matrix exponential used as reference baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference discretization of the PDE; construction of auxiliary variable p and smoother initial condition g(p) in one experiment.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse QFT and measurement/projection onto selected p-state to recover the option price.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Convergence of numerical solution improves as np increases; smoother initial condition yields second-order convergence in p.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; gate complexity ~ O~(T^2 ||u(0)||^3 / (h^4 ε^3 ||u(T)||^3))
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical finite-difference methods / direct ODE solve
speedup_claims.conditions: high-dimensional settings; after choosing Lp = O(log(1/ε)), Np = O(1/ε), and using Schrödingerisation with first-order Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports theoretical scaling and numerical verification on Qiskit, but no wall-clock quantum-vs-classical benchmark on hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: For 1D: ˜O(T^2 ||u(0)||^3 /(h^4 ε^3 ||u(T)||^3)) gate complexity; per-step simulation uses O(Np n_x^2) CNOTs.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical finite-difference methods suffer from curse of dimensionality; paper states classical scaling as O(N_x^d) in general and uses matrix exponential / ODE solve as reference for 1D.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; only small-scale Qiskit statevector simulations with nx=5,6 and np=4,5,6 are reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports polynomial gate complexity and memory savings in theory, but no hardware demonstration or end-to-end runtime advantage over classical methods.
limiting_factors: Classical finite-difference and matrix-exponential baselines are used only as references
Advantage is asymptotic and depends on large problem sizes

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit simulation of the d-dimensional Black-Scholes equation using Schrödingerisation, validated numerically for a 2D cash-or-nothing option example in Qiskit/Matlab-style numerical experiments.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation-based quantum simulation of the d-dimensional Black-Scholes PDE

hyperparameters.correlation_assumption: ρ_mn = 0 for m ≠ n in the main derivation; cross terms discussed as extension

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared from the discretized multi-asset payoff; two initial conditions tested, analogous to the 1D case.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each asset dimension uses an x-register of nx qubits; the auxiliary p-register uses np qubits. The full circuit uses dnx + np qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the d-dimensional Black-Scholes PDE ∂U/∂t + 1/2 Σ_{m,n} σ_m σ_n ρ_mn s_m s_n ∂^2U/(∂s_m∂s_n) + Σ_m r s_m ∂U/∂s_m - rU = 0 after log transform and finite-difference discretization.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Mixed boundary conditions are used; the Schrödingerisation dilation and projection onto a selected p-state recover the original solution.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_BS = A1 ⊗ Dη + A2 ⊗ I^{⊗np} (Hermitian Hamiltonian after Schrödingerisation)

problem_instance.description: Multi-asset Black-Scholes pricing; numerical example is a 2D cash-or-nothing option.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Log-price transform for each asset; finite-difference discretization in each spatial dimension and auxiliary p dimension.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Example 6.2 uses T=1, Δt=10^-3, nx=8, np=7, r=0.03, σ1=σ2=0.3, ρ=0.6, K1=K2=50, x and y on logarithmic intervals, and p∈[-πL, πL] with L=15.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical comparison of the simulated price surface against the exact 2D analytical solution; two initial values are tested and the upper-right region is highlighted; convergence and qualitative agreement are reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference discretization in d spatial dimensions plus auxiliary p dimension; mixed boundary conditions; correlation terms set to zero in the main derivation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse QFT and projection onto selected p-state to recover the multi-asset option price.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Improved agreement with exact solution as np increases; smoother initial condition improves convergence.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; gate complexity ~ O~(d T^2 ||U(0)||^3 Σ c_m^2 / (h^4 ε^3 ||U(T)||^3))
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical finite-difference methods / curse of dimensionality
speedup_claims.conditions: d-dimensional setting with ρ_mn = 0 for m ≠ n in the main derivation; cross terms discussed separately
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper provides theoretical scaling and a 2D numerical example, but no explicit quantum-vs-classical runtime comparison.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: For d dimensions: ˜O(d T^2 ||U(0)||^3 Σ_{m=1}^d c_m^2 /(h^4 ε^3 ||U(T)||^3)) gate complexity; per-step simulation uses O(d Np n_x^2) CNOTs.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Paper states classical finite-difference methods scale as O(N_x^d) and suffer from curse of dimensionality.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; the reported example is a 2D cash-or-nothing option with nx=8 and np=7 in simulation.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper gives asymptotic gate-count scaling O(d Np n_x^2) per step and ˜O(d/ε^3)-type total scaling, but no empirical advantage over classical solvers.
limiting_factors: No benchmark showing quantum runtime beats classical runtime
Cross terms ρ_mn ≠ 0 are only discussed as an extension

num_qubits inferred from the circuit description as dnx + np qubits.
circuit depth not explicitly quantified; only Trotterized circuit structure and gate-count scaling are given.

experiments.description: 1D Black-Scholes Schrödingerisation circuit experiments with two different initial conditions: the direct discretized payoff initial state and the smoother auxiliary initial function g(p).

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation-based quantum simulation of the 1D Black-Scholes PDE with smoother auxiliary initial condition
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Smoother auxiliary initial function g(p) used instead of the direct e^{-|p|} initialization.

key_results: Table 6.1 reports improved L2 convergence for the smoother initial condition: 2.925e-01, 7.540e-02, 2.060e-02 with observed orders 1.96 and 1.88.
The paper states the smoother initial condition yields second-order convergence in p.
